item.title: Said & Checked, Crime and Policing, 2026-11-20: none false or contradicted, 5 unsettled (Thomas Massie)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Thomas Massie, U.S. Representative: “we now know there were over 3 million files” Unsettled. The Justice Department's Jan. 30, 2026 release says it published over 3 million additional pages, for a total production of nearly 3.5 million pages, plus more than 2,000 videos and 180,000 images. The count is of pages, not files, so the figure matches only if files is read loosely as pages.
  • Thomas Massie, U.S. Representative: “I, myself, asked the FBI Director, in a Judiciary Committee hearing: ``Have you found any evidence in there of co-conspirators?''” Unsettled. In the Sept. 17, 2025 Judiciary hearing with FBI Director Kash Patel, Massie asked about men named in FBI interview records and whether investigations had been opened, but the quoted question about co-conspirators does not appear in his questioning in that transcript; other hearings were not read.
  • Thomas Massie, U.S. Representative: “We saw two dozen CEOs resign in the face of these files with no prosecutions.” Unsettled. NBC News's tracker and AP coverage list several senior executives who resigned or stepped back after the releases, including Hyatt's chairman and Goldman Sachs's chief legal officer, and no new U.S. charges, but no source read gives a count near two dozen chief executives.
